turnaround_reason: FMC's crop-protection business was hit by a multi-quarter channel destocking cycle plus generic competition, cratering the stock ~60%+ to ~$11 near its 52-week low. Management suspended the dividend and cut guidance; the bull case is a demand normalization as destocking ends, led by Latin America.
bullish_points: Deep-value optics: P/B ~0.83, fwd P/E ~6.7, trading near 52-week low ($9.95)
Positive free cash flow (~$166M TTM) despite the downturn; management prioritizing cash generation
Destocking is a cyclical (not secular) headwind -- volumes should mean-revert as channel inventory clears
New-active-ingredient pipeline positioned to offset patent cliffs and generics
Latin America demand recovery is the identified swing factor for the rebound
bearish_points: Balance sheet is stretched: debt/equity ~265, total debt ~$4.4B vs ~$477M cash
TTM profit margin -85% and revenue -17.5% YoY -- deep operational damage, not yet stabilized
Dividend suspension is a negative confidence signal, not a bottoming tell
'Basing' screen: bottom is unconfirmed and re-breakdown risk is real if ag markets stay soft
EV/EBITDA ~19.7 shows depressed earnings make it far less cheap on enterprise value than the P/E suggests
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings showing destocking has troughed and Latin America volumes inflecting
suggested_trade: Small-to-medium starter spot $10.50-11.00 for the cyclical-recovery optionality; hold size back given the leverage until a volume inflection is confirmed.
key_risk: The ag downcycle drags longer than expected and the heavy debt load forces further defensive actions, deepening the drawdown.
would_skip_if: Q3 shows revenue still falling with no LatAm volume improvement, or any sign of covenant/leverage stress.
